title: Choosing a metric: OVL vs. Wasserstein
text: Overlapping Coefficient , two densities f1, f2: OVL(f1,f2)=∫ℝdmin⁡(f1(x),f2(x))dx \text{OVL}(f_1, f_2) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \min\big(f_1(x), f_2(x)\big)\, dx total probability mass two distributions share – bounded [0, 1] construction, regardless d. ovl_metric() evaluates closed form two Gaussian posteriors proportional covariance. 2-Wasserstein distance two Gaussians N(mu1, Sigma1), N(mu2, Sigma2) (wasserstein_metric() computes) closed form (Dowson & Landau, 1982; Olkin & Pukelsheim, 1982): W2=‖μ1−μ2‖22+Tr(Σ1+Σ2−2(Σ11/2Σ2Σ11/2)1/2) W_2 = \sqrt{\lVert \mu_1 - \mu_2 \rVert_2^2 +   \mathrm{Tr}\!\Big(\Sigma_1+\Sigma_2-2\big(\Sigma_1^{1/2}\Sigma_2\Sigma_1^{1/2}\big)^{1/2}\Big)} Unbounded, grows d, use normalized version: W2,norm=W2d W_{2,\text{norm}} = \frac{W_2}{\sqrt{d}} stays close stable distance, instead collapsing (like OVL) growing without bound (like un-normalized W_2).

what: Compute Overlapping Coefficient between Groups — calculate_group_overlaps
title: Compute Overlapping Coefficient between Groups — calculate_group_overlaps
text: Computes symmetric matrix pairwise overlapping coefficients (OVL) every pair groups. two groups sharing underlying kernel matrix (kernel_key, .e. set Input values), posterior covariances \(\Sigma_1 = \Sigma/(\lambda_0+N_1)\) \(\Sigma_2 = \Sigma/(\lambda_0+N_2)\) shared raw kernel matrix \(\Sigma\), \(\Sigma_2 = c\,\Sigma_1\) \(c = \mathrm{scale}_1/\mathrm{scale}_2\). Writing \(D^2 = (\mu_2-\mu_1)^\top\Sigma_1^{-1}(\mu_2-\mu_1)\) \(d\) dimension (number shared IDs), exact Gaussian overlap used: \(c = 1\): $$OVL = 2 \Phi\!\left(-D/2\right)$$ \(c \ne 1\), \(\lambda_1 = D^2/(1-c)^2\), \(\lambda_2 = cD^2/(1-c)^2\), \(t = (D^2 - d(1-c)\ln c)/(1-c)^2\): $$OVL = \begin{cases}       F_{\chi^2_d(\lambda_1)}(ct) + 1 - F_{\chi^2_d(\lambda_2)}(t), & 0<c<1 \\       F_{\chi^2_d(\lambda_2)}(t) + 1 - F_{\chi^2_d(\lambda_1)}(ct), & c>1     \end{cases}$$ Two groups different kernel_key (different sets Input values) share common raw kernel matrix \(\Sigma\), closed-form ratio apply; error raised case. \(c\) exactly 1 close (relative difference 1e-6), \(c \ne 1\) formula becomes numerically unstable (divides \((1-c)^2\)). case warning issued \(c = 1\) formula used instead, \(\Sigma_1\) taken whichever group smaller scale (.e. larger, conservative posterior covariance). Cost: pair groups requires one matrix inversion size \(d \times d\) (\(d\) = number shared IDs), total cost \(O(G^2 d^3)\) \(G\) groups – e.g. 10 groups 400 shared IDs already means 45 inversions 400x400 matrices. warning issued likely slow (see max_groups_warn/max_dim_warn).

what: Generate a Synthetic Dataset with Kernel-Structured Covariance — simu_db_kernel
title: Generate a Synthetic Dataset with Kernel-Structured Covariance — simu_db_kernel
text: Simulate complete training dataset, similar simu_db(), consistent generative model underlying posterior_mean: group, vector Output values across nb_id ids (indexed Input position) drawn jointly multivariate normal distribution whose covariance given kernel applied pairwise (shared, per-id) Input values, plus independent measurement noise. replicate independent draw distribution: $$y_n \mid \mu_g \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_g,\ \Sigma_\theta + \sigma^2 ), \quad n = 1,\dots,N_g$$ \(\Sigma_\theta\) kernel matrix (shared) Input values \(\sigma^2\) var_sample. makes \(\Sigma_\theta\) – just Input values – shared across every group, exactly assumed posterior_mean required calculate_group_overlaps. default (mu_random = FALSE) per-group mean \(\mu_g\) deterministic per-id baseline shifted corresponding element diff_group. Setting mu_random = TRUE instead draws \(\mu_g\) conjugate prior, \(\mu_g \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_0,\ \Sigma_\theta/\lambda_0)\) (plus group shift) – useful validating posterior's frequentist coverage true \(\mu_g\).

title: Generate a Synthetic Dataset with Kernel-Structured Covariance — simu_db_kernel
code: simu_db_kernel(   nb_id = 5,   nb_group = 2,   nb_sample = 5,   nb_dim = 1,   range_output = c(0, 50),   range_input = c(0, 50),   diff_group = 3,   var_sample = 2,   kernel = NULL,   mu_random = FALSE,   mu_0 = NULL,   lambda_0 = 1,   pen_diag = 1e-06,   group_labels = NULL,   integer_input = FALSE,   input_grid = FALSE )

title: Generate a Synthetic Dataset with Kernel-Structured Covariance — simu_db_kernel
text: nb_id integer, indicating number features (ids) data. nb_group integer, indicating number groups/conditions. nb_sample integer vector length nb_group. scalar, groups receive number replicates. vector, element g sets number replicates group g independently, enabling unbalanced designs. nb_dim integer, indicating number Input dimensions per id. Defaults 1 (single scalar Input per id, emitted Input_ID = 1). nb_dim > 1, kernel evaluated directly nb_id x nb_dim matrix positions (isotropic default: single shared length_scale across every dimension, unless kernel ard_kernel() similar). range_input applied independently every dimension (dimension's column positions drawn independently, globally-distinct D-dimensional tuples). range_output 2-element vector; midpoint used default baseline mean (mu_0) mu_0 supplied. range_input 2-element vector, indicating range Input values drawn feature dimension. Ignored integer dimension integer_input = TRUE. diff_group numeric scalar vector length nb_group. scalar, group g receives shift diff_group * (g - 1) (linear dose-response, group 1 = reference). vector, element g absolute offset applied group g, allowing arbitrary non-linear group contrasts. var_sample positive number, variance independent measurement noise added top kernel-induced covariance. kernel kernel object (keRnel package). Defaults variance_kernel(variance = 1) * se_kernel(length_scale = 1) NULL. mu_random TRUE, draw group's mean vector conjugate prior \(\mathcal{N}(\mu_0, \Sigma_\theta/\lambda_0)\) instead deterministic constant baseline. Defaults FALSE. mu_0 Baseline mean shared every id (deterministic case) prior mean (mu_random = TRUE); defaults midpoint range_output. lambda_0 Prior precision scaling (used mu_random = TRUE); must single positive number. Defaults 1. pen_diag Jitter added diagonal kernel-induced covariance matrix numerical stability. Defaults 1e-6. group_labels character numeric vector length nb_group providing custom labels Group column. Defaults NULL, uses "1", "2", ..., "nb_group". integer_input Logical. TRUE, Input values distinct integers drawn [ceiling(range_input[1]), floor(range_input[2])]. FALSE (default), Input values continuous uniform draws. See also input_grid. input_grid Logical. used integer_input = TRUE. FALSE (default), integers sampled uniformly without replacement (random positions). TRUE, integers placed regular grid nb_id evenly spaced positions across integer range (deterministic layout).

title: Generate a Synthetic Dataset with Kernel-Structured Covariance — simu_db_kernel
text: data frame synthetic data columns ID, Group, Sample, Input_ID, Input, Output. Two attributes attached: mu_true Named list, one entry per group, named vector true per-feature means. base_input nb_id x nb_dim numeric matrix (rownames = ID) giving Input position(s) assigned feature.

title: Generate a Synthetic Dataset with Kernel-Structured Covariance — simu_db_kernel
code: # Default kernel (variance = 1, length_scale = 1): data <- simu_db_kernel()  # Custom kernel: ker <- keRnel::variance_kernel(variance = 2) * keRnel::se_kernel(length_scale = 3) data <- simu_db_kernel(kernel = ker)  # Unbalanced design: 3 replicates for group 1, 15 for group 2: data <- simu_db_kernel(nb_sample = c(3, 15))  # Arbitrary group contrasts (non-linear dose-response): data <- simu_db_kernel(nb_group = 4, diff_group = c(0, 5, 5, 10))  # Custom group labels: data <- simu_db_kernel(nb_group = 2, group_labels = c("Control", "Treatment"))  # Integer inputs on a regular grid: data <- simu_db_kernel(nb_id = 10, integer_input = TRUE, input_grid = TRUE,                        range_input = c(0, 100))  # Multi-dimensional Input (D = 2), isotropic kernel: data <- simu_db_kernel(nb_dim = 2)

title: Total Variation Distance — tvd_metric
text: Total variation distance two groups' posteriors, \(TV(f,g) = 1 - \int \min(f,g)\,dx\). general identity two densities (approximation specific Gaussians): since \(\int(f+g)\,dx = 2\), \(\int|f-g|\,dx = 2 - 2\int\min(f,g)\,dx\), \(TV = \tfrac12\int|f-g|\,dx = 1 - \int\min(f,g)\,dx\) always. ovl_metric already computes \(\int\min(f,g)\,dx\) closed form, TVD just 1 -  value – thin decorator around rather new closed-form derivation. Forwards requires_shared_kernel/is_symmetric_metric wrapped metric.
